name: Domaine Sigalas
story: Founded in 1991 by Paris Sigalas in the flat vineyards of Oia, on the north of the island. The domaine is one of the names that made Santorini Assyrtiko famous abroad, working old vines trained in the island's basket-shaped 'kouloura' style.

wines.name: Santorini Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Mineral and salty, with citrus and a long, firm finish.

wines.name: Kavalieros
wines.notes: Single-vineyard Assyrtiko from very old vines; deep and age-worthy.

wines.name: Mavrotragano
wines.notes: A rare red grape of the island: dark fruit and firm tannins.

name: Santo Wines
story: The Union of Santorini Cooperatives, gathering the grapes of over a thousand island growers. Its winery and tasting terrace sit on the caldera edge near Pyrgos.

wines.name: Santo Santorini
wines.notes: Classic Assyrtiko: lemon, flint and sea salt.

wines.name: Santo Nykteri
wines.notes: Traditionally harvested late and oak-aged; richer and rounder.

wines.name: Santo Vinsanto
wines.notes: Sun-dried grapes give raisin, caramel and bright acidity.

wines.name: Santo Selection Cuvée
wines.notes: Selected Santorini Assyrtiko, fuller and more concentrated.

wines.name: Santo Sparkling Brut
wines.notes: Traditional-method sparkling Assyrtiko.

name: Estate Argyros
story: A family estate tracing its winemaking to 1903, with some of the oldest vineyards on the island around Episkopi Gonias. Known for long-aged Vinsanto and serious Assyrtiko.

wines.name: Estate Argyros Assyrtiko
wines.notes: From very old vines; concentrated, mineral, long-lived.

wines.name: Argyros Vinsanto
wines.notes: Aged for years in oak: dried fig, coffee and spice.

wines.name: Argyros Mavrotragano
wines.notes: Dark, spicy island red.

wines.name: Cuvée Monsignori
wines.notes: Old-vine Santorini Assyrtiko, powerful and long.

wines.name: Cuvée Palatia
wines.notes: Balanced Assyrtiko with a long, fresh finish.

name: Hatzidakis Winery
story: Started in 1997 by Haridimos Hatzidakis, a winery partly dug into the volcanic rock near Pyrgos. Farmed organically, it became a cult name for intense, natural-leaning Santorini wines.

wines.name: Santorini Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Powerful, saline and textured.

wines.name: Nykteri
wines.notes: Fuller-bodied traditional style with ripe citrus and nuts.

wines.name: Aidani
wines.notes: Floral and gentle, from another native island grape.

wines.name: Familia
wines.notes: The winery's 'simplest' Santorini, still age-worthy.

wines.name: Cuvée No. 15
wines.notes: Tiny-production, low-intervention Assyrtiko.

name: Venetsanos Winery
story: Built in 1947 by the Venetsanos family above the port of Athinios, it was Santorini's first industrial winery. The multi-level building was designed to move wine by gravity, and its terrace looks straight over the caldera. After decades closed, the winery was brought back to life and reopened in 2014.

wines.name: Santorini Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Crisp and saline, typical of the volcanic soil.

wines.name: Nykteri
wines.notes: Oak-aged traditional style, rounder and nutty.

wines.name: Vinsanto
wines.notes: Sweet wine from sun-dried grapes.

name: Gaia Wines Santorini
story: Gaia's island winery is housed in a stone tomato-processing factory from the early 1900s, right on the beach on the east coast. It focuses on Assyrtiko from old, own-rooted vines.

wines.name: Thalassitis
wines.notes: Their flagship Assyrtiko: lemon, flint and sea spray.

wines.name: Assyrtiko Wild Ferment
wines.notes: Fermented with natural yeasts, partly in oak; layered and textured.

wines.name: Vinsanto
wines.notes: Traditional sweet wine of the island.

wines.name: Thalassitis Submerged
wines.notes: Rare Assyrtiko aged for years on the Aegean sea bed.

name: Artemis Karamolegos Winery
story: A family winery between Kamari and Mesaria, run by Artemis Karamolegos, the third generation of a winemaking family. It has grown into one of the island's most respected producers, with a restaurant among the vines.

wines.name: Santorini Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Bright, mineral and saline.

wines.name: Pyritis
wines.notes: Old-vine Assyrtiko with great concentration.

wines.name: Nykteri
wines.notes: Traditional oak-aged style.

name: Boutari Santorini Winery
story: Boutari began exploring Santorini's vineyards in the late 1980s and made its first harvest at Megalochori in 1989; Santorini Boutari helped make Assyrtiko famous abroad. In September 2024 the historic Megalochori winery was bought by Alpha Estate (Ktima Alfa).

wines.name: Santorini
wines.notes: Classic, crisp Assyrtiko.

wines.name: Kallisti
wines.notes: Barrel-fermented Assyrtiko, rounder and richer.

wines.name: Vinsanto
wines.notes: Sweet wine from sun-dried grapes.

name: Gaia Estate
story: Founded in 1994 by oenologist Yiannis Paraskevopoulos and Leon Karatsalos, with vineyards high on the hills of Koutsi. Gaia helped show how elegant Agiorgitiko from Nemea can be.

wines.name: Gaia Estate
wines.notes: Their top Agiorgitiko: dark cherry, spice and fine tannins.

wines.name: Agiorgitiko by Gaia
wines.notes: Juicy, fresh red fruit, easy to love.

wines.name: Notios Red
wines.notes: Bright, everyday Agiorgitiko blend.

name: Domaine Skouras
story: Founded in 1986 by George Skouras, a Dijon-trained oenologist and one of the pioneers of modern Greek wine. Based near Argos, it works with Agiorgitiko and Moschofilero alongside international grapes.

wines.name: Megas Oenos
wines.notes: Agiorgitiko with Cabernet Sauvignon; structured and age-worthy.

wines.name: Grande Cuvée Nemea
wines.notes: Rich, oak-aged Agiorgitiko.

wines.name: Moschofilero
wines.notes: Floral and fresh, from the Arcadian highlands.

name: Papaioannou Estate
story: A family estate in Ancient Nemea led by Thanasis Papaioannou, a pioneer of the region and among the first to farm organically and bottle Nemea from single plots. Its 'Palea Klimata', from Agiorgitiko vines over 40 years old, paved the way for age-worthy Nemea reds.

wines.name: Palea Klimata Nemea
wines.notes: From old vines: deep, spicy and long.

wines.name: Nemea Agiorgitiko
wines.notes: Classic plum and sweet spice.

wines.name: Moschofilero
wines.notes: Light and aromatic.

name: Palivou Estate
story: Started in 1995 by George Palivos in Ancient Nemea, close to the archaeological site, and now run with his daughters Vasiliki and Evangelia. The family farms about 30 hectares across the Nemea zone and was among the first to open its winery to visitors. Agiorgitiko is the focus, from fresh to oak-aged.

wines.name: Nemea Agiorgitiko
wines.notes: Ripe red fruit with gentle oak.

wines.name: Terra Leone
wines.notes: Their top selection of Agiorgitiko.
Kydonitsa with wild yeasts and 4 months in oak: citrus, peach and honey.
wines.name: Diaselo Kydonitsa Wild Yeast

name: Semeli Winery
story: Semeli began in Attica and later built a modern winery in the hills of Nemea, with views over the vineyards. It makes Agiorgitiko from fresh to reserve styles.

wines.name: Semeli Nemea Reserve
wines.notes: Oak-aged Agiorgitiko: plum, vanilla and spice.

wines.name: Mountain Sun
wines.notes: Fresh, fruity Agiorgitiko.

wines.name: Mountain Sun White
wines.notes: Light, aromatic white blend.

wines.name: Semeli Nemea Grande Reserve
wines.notes: Top Agiorgitiko from Koutsi at 650 m: 18 months in new oak, 24 in bottle.

name: Domaine Tselepos
story: Founded in 1989 by Yiannis Tselepos on the high plateau of Arcadia. It is one of the leading names for Mantinia Moschofilero and also makes sparkling wine and a celebrated Merlot.

wines.name: Mantinia Moschofilero
wines.notes: Rose petal, citrus and lively acidity.

wines.name: Kokkinomylos Merlot
wines.notes: Single-vineyard Merlot, rich and polished.

wines.name: Amalia Brut
wines.notes: Traditional-method sparkling wine from Moschofilero.

name: Troupis Winery
story: A family winery in the Fteri area of the Mantinia plateau, about 700 m high. Its 'Fteri' labels, launched in 2010, put Troupis on the map with pure, aromatic Moschofilero.

wines.name: Fteri Moschofilero
wines.notes: Intensely floral: jasmine, rose and citrus.

wines.name: Fteri Agiorgitiko
wines.notes: Light, juicy red; lovely slightly chilled.

wines.name: Fteri Rosé
wines.notes: Fresh and fragrant.

name: Domaine Spiropoulos
story: Five generations of the Spiropoulos family have grown vines in mountainous Arcadia. Their modern winery opened in Ancient Mantinia in 1991 and all family vineyards have been certified organic since 1994; a second winery followed in Nemea in 2007. Best known for Moschofilero in still and sparkling styles.

wines.name: Mantinia Moschofilero
wines.notes: Aromatic, light and crisp.

wines.name: Ode Panos
wines.notes: Sparkling Moschofilero, fresh and floral.

name: Monemvasia Winery
story: Founded by the Tsimbidis family near the medieval castle town of Monemvasia. It revived the historic local grapes behind the famous Malvasia wines of the Middle Ages. The first modern Monemvasia-Malvasia, from the 2010 harvest, was bottled after 17 years of effort.

wines.name: Monemvasia-Malvasia
wines.notes: Revival of the historic sweet wine: dried fruit, honey and spice.

wines.name: Kydonitsa
wines.notes: Quince-scented local white grape.

wines.name: Mavroudi
wines.notes: Rare Laconian red variety.

wines.name: Monemvasia White
wines.notes: Dry white from the local Monemvasia grape: pear, apricot and flowers.

name: Tetramythos Winery
story: Set in the mountains above the Gulf of Corinth, Tetramythos farms high vineyards organically. It is known for fresh Roditis and for reviving the rare Mavro Kalavrytino grape.

wines.name: Roditis
wines.notes: Crisp, lemony mountain white.

wines.name: Malagousia
wines.notes: Aromatic: peach and jasmine.

wines.name: Black of Kalavryta
wines.notes: Light, spicy red from a rare local grape.

name: Parparoussis Winery
story: Founded in 1974 at Bozaitika, Patras, to make quality bottled wines. The family is respected for bringing out the best of local grapes such as Sideritis, Mavrodaphne and Muscat of Rio.

wines.name: Sideritis Dons de Dionysos
wines.notes: Delicate, fresh white from a rare pink-skinned grape.

wines.name: Taos Mavrodaphne
wines.notes: A dry Mavrodaphne: dark fruit and spice.

wines.name: Mavrodaphne of Patras
wines.notes: The classic sweet red of Patras.

name: Rouvalis Winery (Oenoforos)
story: Founded by oenologist Angelos Rouvalis in the mountains above Aigio. Its Roditis from high-altitude, stony vineyards helped change how Greeks saw the grape.

wines.name: Asprolithi
wines.notes: Roditis from stony mountain vineyards, first released in 1990: crisp, citrusy and mineral.

wines.name: Lagorthi
wines.notes: Rare local grape, citrusy and fresh.

name: Mercouri Estate
story: A historic family estate founded in 1864 near Pyrgos in western Peloponnese, with a 19th-century manor, gardens and a small museum. Known for its Refosco and Mavrodaphne red.

wines.name: Domaine Mercouri Red
wines.notes: Refosco with Mavrodaphne: dark fruit and herbs.

wines.name: Foloi
wines.notes: Roditis with Viognier, fresh and aromatic.

wines.name: Mercouri Cava
wines.notes: 80% Refosco, 20% Mavrodaphne from the estate's best plots; aged and complex.

name: Achaia Clauss
story: Founded in 1861 by the Bavarian Gustav Clauss on a hill above Patras. Its stone cellars hold old barrels of Mavrodaphne, the region's famous sweet red, and the estate is a popular place to visit. Clauss first made his sweet red in 1873 and named it Mavrodaphne, after Daphne, a dark-eyed young woman from Patras.

wines.name: Mavrodaphne of Patras
wines.notes: Sweet fortified red: raisin, chocolate and coffee.

wines.name: Demestica
wines.notes: One of Greece's best-known everyday wines.

wines.name: Mavrodaphne "601" Reserve
wines.notes: Long-aged Mavrodaphne named after page 601 of Clauss's recipe book.

wines.name: Mavrodaphne Grand Reserve
wines.notes: Very old Mavrodaphne from the historic cellars.

name: Papagiannakos Winery
story: A family winery in Markopoulo, near Athens airport, founded in 1919 and now run by the third generation, Vassilis Papagiannakos. He was among the first to believe in Savatiano as a fine, age-worthy wine.

wines.name: Savatiano
wines.notes: Fresh citrus and herbs, the wine of Athens.

wines.name: Vientzi Savatiano
wines.notes: Single-vineyard Savatiano that ages beautifully.

wines.name: Malagousia
wines.notes: Aromatic, peachy white.
Old-vine Savatiano with four months in oak: lemon, coconut and vanilla.
wines.name: Savatiano Vareli

name: Mylonas Winery
story: Started in 1917 by grandfather Antonis, who made Savatiano in clay jars in Keratea, East Attica. Today brothers Stamatis, Antonis and Tasos run a small modern winery focused on old-vine Savatiano.

wines.name: Savatiano
wines.notes: Crisp apple and ripe lemon.

wines.name: Naked Truth
wines.notes: Orange-style Savatiano made with skin contact.

wines.name: Retsina
wines.notes: Traditional pine-resin wine, fresh and herbal.
Old-vine Savatiano built to age: ripe fruit and crisp acidity.
wines.name: Cuvée Vouno Savatiano

name: Kir-Yianni
story: Founded in 1997 by Yiannis Boutaris on the slopes of Mount Vermio. A leading name for Xinomavro, with vineyards in Naoussa and Amyndeo.

wines.name: Ramnista
wines.notes: Xinomavro with cherry, tomato leaf and fine tannins.

wines.name: Diaporos
wines.notes: Xinomavro with Syrah from a single vineyard; deep and spicy.

wines.name: Samaropetra
wines.notes: Fresh, aromatic white from Amyndeo.

name: Boutari Winery
story: The Boutari family started making wine in Naoussa in 1879, and its Naoussa red is one of the best-known Greek wines. The winery offers tours and tastings.

wines.name: Naoussa
wines.notes: Classic Xinomavro: sour cherry, spice and firm tannins.

wines.name: Grande Reserve Naoussa
wines.notes: Long-aged Xinomavro with leather and dried fruit.

name: Thymiopoulos Vineyards
story: Apostolos Thymiopoulos farms biodynamically in Trilofo and Fytia, on the southern side of the Naoussa appellation. His wines show a softer, fruitier side of Xinomavro.

wines.name: Earth & Sky (Gi kai Ouranos)
wines.notes: Ripe, perfumed Xinomavro with fine tannins.

wines.name: Uranos
wines.notes: Old-vine single-plot Xinomavro.

wines.name: Young Vines
wines.notes: Juicy, fresh Xinomavro.

name: Domaine Dalamara
story: The Dalamaras family has made wine in Naoussa since 1840. Since 2000 the winery has been run by Kostis Dalamaras, the sixth generation, with organic vineyards, native yeasts and a fresh, pure style of Xinomavro.

wines.name: Naoussa
wines.notes: Elegant, classic Xinomavro.

wines.name: Paliokalias
wines.notes: Single-vineyard Naoussa, structured and long-lived.

name: Alpha Estate
story: Founded in 1997 by Makis Mavridis and oenologist Angelos Iatridis on the cool, sandy plateau of Amyndeo, about 700 m high. Famous for old-vine Xinomavro and its modern blends.

wines.name: Xinomavro Reserve Vieilles Vignes
wines.notes: From ungrafted old vines; deep and age-worthy.

wines.name: Hedgehog Xinomavro
wines.notes: Single-vineyard Xinomavro, bright and spicy.

wines.name: Alpha Estate Sauvignon Blanc
wines.notes: Crisp, aromatic and fresh.

name: Karanika
story: Started by Laurens Hartman and Annette van Zijl in cool, high Amyndeo. They specialise in traditional-method sparkling wine from Xinomavro and Assyrtiko.

wines.name: Brut Cuvée Spéciale
wines.notes: Traditional-method sparkling, mostly Xinomavro: fine bubbles, citrus, toast and hazelnut.

wines.name: Brut Rosé
wines.notes: Sparkling Xinomavro, red berries and freshness.

name: Ktima Gerovassiliou
story: Founded in 1981 by oenologist Evangelos Gerovassiliou on the coastal hills of Epanomi. He saved the Malagousia grape from near extinction, and the estate also has a well-known wine museum.

wines.name: Malagousia
wines.notes: Peach, jasmine and citrus; the wine that revived the grape.

wines.name: Ktima Gerovassiliou White
wines.notes: Assyrtiko with Malagousia: fresh and aromatic.

wines.name: Avaton
wines.notes: Blend of rare local reds: dark fruit and spice.

wines.name: Ktima Gerovassiliou Red
wines.notes: Syrah, Merlot and Limnio: one of Greece's best-known reds.

wines.name: Malagousia Late Harvest
wines.notes: Sweet wine from overripe Malagousia: honey, ripe fruit and nuts.

name: Domaine Kechris
story: A family winery near Thessaloniki that turned retsina into a fine wine. Its 'Tear of the Pine', made from Assyrtiko grown in Goumenissa and aged in barrel with a touch of pine resin, showed that retsina can be elegant and age-worthy.

wines.name: Tear of the Pine
wines.notes: Assyrtiko retsina with pine, citrus and herbs.

wines.name: Kechribari
wines.notes: Classic retsina, light and refreshing.

name: Domaine Porto Carras
story: Created in the 1960s by shipowner John Carras, with vineyards on the slopes of Mount Meliton running down towards the sea. A landmark estate of northern Greece.

wines.name: Château Porto Carras
wines.notes: Bordeaux-style blend, structured and age-worthy.

wines.name: Limnio
wines.notes: An ancient Greek grape: herbs and red fruit.

wines.name: Malagouzia
wines.notes: Aromatic, fresh white.

name: Tsantali
story: Founded in 1890 by Evangelos Tsantalis, today one of Greece's largest wine companies. It also works vineyards on Mount Athos and in Rapsani on Mount Olympus.

wines.name: Rapsani Reserve
wines.notes: Xinomavro, Krassato and Stavroto from Mount Olympus.

wines.name: Agioritikos
wines.notes: Wine from the vineyards of Mount Athos.

name: Biblia Chora
story: Founded in 1998 by oenologists Vassilis Tsaktsarlis and Vangelis Gerovassiliou on the slopes of Mount Pangeo, at Kokkinochori near Kavala. The vineyard is farmed organically, and its fresh white blends became modern Greek classics.

wines.name: Biblia Chora White
wines.notes: Sauvignon Blanc with Assyrtiko: crisp and aromatic.

wines.name: Ovilos
wines.notes: Semillon and Assyrtiko, rich and oak-aged.

wines.name: Areti
wines.notes: Single-variety Assyrtiko.

name: Ktima Pavlidis
story: Created in 1998 by Christoforos Pavlidis, who searched for years before choosing this spot in Kokkinogia, Drama, for his vineyard and winery. Its 'Thema' white became one of Greece's best-selling quality wines.

wines.name: Thema White
wines.notes: Assyrtiko with Sauvignon Blanc: fresh and aromatic.

wines.name: Thema Red
wines.notes: Agiorgitiko with Syrah: round and fruity.

name: Domaine Costa Lazaridi
story: Founded by Costas Lazaridis in Drama, with a striking winery and visitor centre. Its 'Amethystos' range is one of the best-known Greek wine labels.

wines.name: Amethystos Red
wines.notes: Cabernet-based blend, rich and round.

wines.name: Amethystos White
wines.notes: Fresh blend with Sauvignon Blanc and Assyrtiko.

wines.name: Château Julia Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Crisp, citrusy Assyrtiko.

wines.name: Amethystos Cava
wines.notes: Long-aged Cabernet Franc-based red, the top of the Amethystos range.

name: Wine Art Estate (Ktima Techni Oinou)
story: A boutique winery in Drama focused on careful, terroir-driven wines. Its 'Techni Alipias' blend is a favourite of Greek wine lovers.

wines.name: Techni Alipias White
wines.notes: Sauvignon Blanc with Assyrtiko: crisp and lively.

wines.name: Plano Malagousia
wines.notes: Aromatic, fresh Malagousia.

name: Ktima Chatzivaritis
story: A family estate in Goumenissa, at the foot of Mount Paiko, farmed organically. Goumenissa blends Xinomavro with the softer Negoska grape.

wines.name: Goumenissa
wines.notes: 70% Xinomavro, 30% Negoska, 12 months in French oak: red berries, cherry and spice.

wines.name: Negoska
wines.notes: Soft, fruity local grape.

name: Domaine Tatsis
story: Brothers Periklis and Stergios Tatsis make low-intervention wines in Goumenissa, from organic vineyards. A pioneer of natural wine in Greece.

wines.name: Goumenissa
wines.notes: Xinomavro and Negoska, natural style.

wines.name: Malagousia
wines.notes: Skin-contact, textured white.

wines.name: Old Roots Xinomavro
wines.notes: Xinomavro from old vines, natural style.

name: Domaine Glinavos
story: Founded by Lefteris Glinavos, who studied winemaking in France and returned to his home village of Zitsa. Known for sparkling and semi-sparkling wines from the local Debina grape. Naoussa winemaker Apostolos Thymiopoulos has recently invested in the estate, keeping the Glinavos name.

wines.name: Zitsa Brut
wines.notes: Light, crisp sparkling Debina.

wines.name: Paleokerisio
wines.notes: Semi-sparkling, slightly sweet orange wine: a cult classic.
Still Debina, wild-yeast fermented and 10 months on lees; elegant and fresh.
wines.name: Fine Debina

name: Katogi Averoff
story: Founded by politician Evangelos Averoff in the mountain town of Metsovo, where he replanted vines in the 1950s. Its Katogi red was one of the first modern Greek wines.

wines.name: Katogi Averoff
wines.notes: Cabernet Sauvignon 40%, Merlot 30%, Agiorgitiko 30%, a year in oak: red fruit, spice and leather.

wines.name: Traminer
wines.notes: Aromatic white from a high-altitude vineyard.

name: Domaine Zafeirakis
story: A family winery in Tyrnavos, Thessaly, known for reviving the local Limniona grape. Christos Zafeirakis, the fifth generation, studied oenology in Milan, made his first Limniona in 2008 and farms all the vineyards organically.

wines.name: Limniona
wines.notes: Fresh red fruit and herbs, elegant.

wines.name: Malagousia
wines.notes: Fragrant, fresh white.

name: Lyrarakis Wines
story: A family winery founded in 1966 at Alagni, in the hills south of Heraklion. The Lyrarakis family brought forgotten Cretan grapes such as Plyto and Dafni back to life; Dafni was saved by planting it in the Psarades vineyard at 480 m in the early 1990s.

wines.name: Dafni
wines.notes: Herbal, bay-leaf aromas from a rare Cretan grape.

wines.name: Plyto
wines.notes: Light, lemony and saline.

wines.name: Vilana
wines.notes: Fresh, everyday Cretan white.

name: Douloufakis Winery
story: A family winery in Dafnes since 1930, now run by the third generation. It is known for Vidiano and the local Liatiko red.

wines.name: Dafnios Vidiano
wines.notes: Apricot, herbs and a round texture.

wines.name: Dafnios Red
wines.notes: Liatiko: light, spicy Cretan red.
Barrel-aged Vidiano: stone fruit, white flowers, vanilla and nuts; the wine that put Vidiano on the map.
wines.name: Aspros Lagos Vidiano

name: Idaia Winery
story: Founded by oenologists Vassilis Laderos and Kalliopi Volitaki in Venerato, below Mount Ida, inside the Dafnes appellation. The family winery makes about 130,000 bottles a year from native Cretan grapes, especially Vidiano and Thrapsathiri.

wines.name: Vidiano
wines.notes: Stone fruit and herbs, full and fresh.

wines.name: Thrapsathiri
wines.notes: Lemony, light and refreshing.

name: Domaine Paterianakis
story: Founded in 1988 by Giorgos Paterianakis at Melesses, in the Peza zone south-east of Heraklion, and one of Crete's organic pioneers. Today sisters Emmanouela and Niki, the third generation, run the certified-organic estate, making wines from local grapes such as Vidiano and Kotsifali.

wines.name: Vidiano
wines.notes: Round, aromatic Cretan white.

wines.name: Kotsifali
wines.notes: Soft, spicy local red.

name: Domaine Economou
story: Yiannis Economou returned to Crete in 1994 after working in Germany, Bordeaux (Château Margaux) and Piedmont. On the high Ziros plateau in eastern Crete he farms mostly own-rooted native vines and releases his long-aged, traditional Sitia wines only when he thinks they are ready.

wines.name: Sitia
wines.notes: Liatiko with Mandilari, aged for years before release.

wines.name: Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Mineral and textured.

name: Manousakis Winery
story: Ted Manousakis came home to Vatolakkos near Chania in 1993 and planted Rhône varieties; 'Nostos' means homecoming. His daughter Alexandra has made the wines since 2007, and the vineyards are certified organic.

wines.name: Nostos Blend
wines.notes: Syrah, Grenache and Mourvèdre: ripe and spicy.

wines.name: Nostos Roussanne
wines.notes: Rich, textured white.

name: Domaine Sclavos
story: A small family estate on the Paliki peninsula in western Kefalonia, run since 2015 by Evriviadis (Vladis) Sclavos and Spiros Zisimatos. Biodynamic farming, native yeasts and minimal sulfites; some vines are ungrafted survivors of phylloxera.

wines.notes: 'Wine of the stone': salty, mineral Robola from limestone slopes, made with minimal intervention.
wines.name: Vino di Sasso Robola
Mavrodaphne
wines.notes: Dry red from the island grape.

name: Gentilini Winery
story: Founded in 1984 on Kefalonia and known early on for pioneering winemaking on the island. Since 2002 Petros Markantonatos has led the estate and moved it toward organic farming. Robola comes from high, stony vineyards on Mount Ainos at 650 m and above.

wines.name: Gentilini Robola
wines.notes: Lemon, flint and freshness.

wines.name: Eclipse
wines.notes: Mavrodaphne-based dry red.
Robola from their oldest vineyard at 850 m, part barrel-fermented: mineral and complex with age.
wines.name: Robola Wild Paths

name: Robola Cooperative of Kefalonia
story: Orealios Gaea, the Robola cooperative of Kefalonia, was founded in 1982 and brings together about 300 growers. Their San Gerasimo Robola comes from mountain vineyards on the slopes of Mount Ainos, at up to 800 m.

wines.name: Robola of Kefalonia
wines.notes: Fresh, citrusy island white.

name: Moraitis Winery
story: A family winery on Paros, making wine since 1910. Its old stone cellars in Naoussa host a small museum and tastings.

wines.name: Monemvasia
wines.notes: Local grape: fresh and herbal.

wines.name: Mandilaria
wines.notes: Island red with dark fruit.
A special, salty, intense Monemvasia from old vines.
wines.name: Thapsana

name: T-Oinos
story: A small winery on the granite plateau of Tinos, among huge boulders. It quickly gained international praise for its Assyrtiko and Mavrotragano.

wines.name: Clos Stegasta Assyrtiko
wines.notes: Granite-grown Assyrtiko: tense and mineral.

wines.name: Mavrotragano
wines.notes: Rare island red, deep and spicy.

name: Emery Winery
story: One of Rhodes' oldest wineries, founded in 1923 in the mountain village of Embonas and named after Emery d'Amboise, a Grand Master of the Knights of St John. The Triantafillou family runs it, working the local Athiri and Amorgiano (Mandilaria) grapes from the slopes of Mount Attaviros.

wines.name: Villare
wines.notes: Athiri: delicate, lemony and floral.

wines.name: Grand Rosé
wines.notes: Fresh island rosé.

name: Samos Wine Cooperative (UVS)
story: The Union of Winemaking Cooperatives of Samos gathers the island's growers, who farm white Muscat on steep mountain terraces. Its Vin Doux, a fortified sweet Muscat, made Samos wines famous around the world.

wines.name: Samos Vin Doux
wines.notes: Golden, honeyed Muscat.

wines.name: Samos Nectar
wines.notes: Made from sun-dried grapes: rich and aged.

wines.name: Samos Anthemis
wines.notes: Oak-aged Muscat, deep and complex.

name: Château Lune Douce
story: A classic Left Bank château whose gravel soils give perfumed Cabernet Sauvignon. The cellar still uses its original oak vats.

wines.name: Grand Vin
wines.notes: Cassis, cedar and violet with fine-grained tannins.

wines.name: Second Lune
wines.notes: Younger vines, more open fruit, drink in 5 years.

wines.name: Bordeaux Blanc
wines.notes: Sauvignon–Sémillon, citrus and beeswax.

events.title: En primeur preview
events.desc: Taste the 2026 vintage from barrel.

name: Clos des Pierres
story: Limestone caves beneath the vineyard keep the wine cool all year. Merlot-led wines with a touch of Cabernet Franc.

wines.name: Clos des Pierres
wines.notes: Plush plum, truffle and mocha.

wines.name: Les Caves
wines.notes: Fresh, juicy, ready now.

wines.name: Crémant de Bordeaux
wines.notes: Fine bubbles, green apple and brioche.

events.title: Candlelit cave tour
events.desc: Walk the limestone caves by candlelight, three tastings.

name: Domaine Côte d'Ambre
story: Eight generations tending tiny parcels of Pinot Noir. Every climat is vinified separately to show its soil.

wines.name: Gevrey-Chambertin
wines.notes: Dark cherry, earth and spice.

wines.name: Bourgogne Rouge
wines.notes: Bright raspberry, easy and pure.

wines.name: Aligoté
wines.notes: Zesty, perfect for kir.

events.title: Saint-Vincent Tournante
events.desc: Join Burgundy's winter wine festival from our courtyard.

name: Maison Perlée
story: Four kilometres of chalk cellars beneath the Avenue de Champagne hold millions of bottles ageing on their lees.

wines.name: Brut Réserve
wines.notes: Toasted brioche, pear and fine mousse.

wines.name: Blanc de Blancs 2016
wines.notes: Pure Chardonnay, lemon curd and chalk.

wines.name: Rosé Saignée
wines.notes: Wild strawberry, deep colour, gastronomic.

events.title: New Year's Eve cellar party
events.desc: Midnight toast 30 metres underground.

events.title: Disgorging workshop
events.desc: Open your own bottle 'à la volée' and take it home.

name: Bodegas Río Oja
story: Built next to the old railway station of Haro so barrels could ship to Bordeaux during phylloxera. Long ageing in American oak is the house style.

wines.name: Gran Reserva
wines.notes: Dried cherry, leather, vanilla, silky.

wines.name: Crianza
wines.notes: Fresh red fruit with a touch of oak.

wines.name: Viura Blanco
wines.notes: Crisp and herbal.

events.title: Tapas & Tempranillo night
events.desc: Pintxos from Haro's best bars with our reservas.

name: Quinta do Socalco
story: Schist terraces drop steeply to the river. Grapes are still foot-trodden in granite lagares for the Port.

wines.name: 20 Year Tawny
wines.notes: Walnut, orange peel and caramel.

wines.name: Vintage Port 2017
wines.notes: Blackberry and violets, decades ahead.

wines.name: Douro Tinto
wines.notes: Touriga Nacional, bold and floral.

events.title: River boat & Port tasting
events.desc: Rabelo boat trip with lunch at the quinta.

name: Fattoria del Cipresso
story: An old farmhouse among cypresses and olive groves. Sangiovese is aged in large Slavonian casks, never small new barrels.

wines.name: Chianti Classico Riserva
wines.notes: Sour cherry, tea leaf and dried herbs.

wines.name: Gran Selezione
wines.notes: Single vineyard, deep and structured.

wines.name: Vin Santo
wines.notes: Hazelnut and dried apricot, for cantucci.

events.title: New olive oil & wine day
events.desc: Fresh 'olio nuovo' on bruschetta with this year's wine.

name: Cascina Nebbia
story: Named after the autumn fog that gives Nebbiolo its name. A tiny estate making only three wines, all from the same hill.

wines.name: Barolo
wines.notes: Tar and roses, firm tannins.

wines.name: Langhe Nebbiolo
wines.notes: A gentler Barolo, ready younger.

wines.name: Dolcetto d'Alba
wines.notes: Everyday red, plum and almond.

events.title: White truffle dinner
events.desc: Five courses with Alba truffle and our Barolo verticals.

name: Weingut Steilhang
story: Riesling vines on slate slopes so steep they are worked by hand with winches. Low alcohol, high tension.

wines.name: Riesling Kabinett
wines.notes: Off-dry, green apple and slate.

wines.name: Riesling GG
wines.notes: Dry, peach and smoke.

wines.name: Eiswein
wines.notes: Grapes frozen on the vine: pure, electric sweetness.

events.title: Christmas market wine stand
events.desc: Glühwein made from our Riesling at the village market.

name: Aszú Pince
story: Mould-covered tunnels carved into volcanic tuff. Tokaji Aszú, 'wine of kings, king of wines', is made from botrytised berries.

wines.name: Tokaji Aszú 6 Puttonyos
wines.notes: Apricot, saffron and electric acidity.

wines.name: Furmint Dry
wines.notes: Quince, smoke, mineral.

wines.name: Szamorodni
wines.notes: Nutty, sherry-like, dry.

events.title: Cellar labyrinth tour
events.desc: Explore 17th-century tunnels with candle and glass.

name: Qvevri House
story: Wine is fermented in clay qvevri buried underground, an 8,000-year-old method listed by UNESCO.

wines.name: Rkatsiteli Amber
wines.notes: Skin-contact white: dried apricot, tea, grip.

wines.name: Saperavi
wines.notes: Inky purple, blackberry and pepper.

wines.name: Mtsvane
wines.notes: Floral, honey and walnut.

events.title: Supra feast
events.desc: Traditional Georgian table with toasts led by a tamada.

name: Oak Knoll Ridge
story: Planted the year California beat France at the Judgment of Paris. Hillside Cabernet with views across the valley.

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.notes: Blackcurrant, mocha, polished tannins.

wines.name: Chardonnay
wines.notes: Ripe pear, butter and toasted oak.

wines.name: Sauvignon Blanc
wines.notes: Grapefruit and fresh-cut grass.

events.title: Holiday open house
events.desc: Library wines, live jazz and wood-fired pizza.

name: Fog Line Vineyards
story: Cool ocean fog rolls in each afternoon, giving slow-ripened Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

wines.name: Pinot Noir
wines.notes: Raspberry, forest floor, silky.

wines.name: Blanc de Noirs
wines.notes: Crisp red-apple bubbles.

wines.name: Coastal Chardonnay
wines.notes: Lean and saline.

events.title: Crab & Pinot weekend
events.desc: Dungeness crab season meets our Pinot Noir.

name: Red Hills Cellars
story: Volcanic red Jory soil and a small, organic farm. Pinot Noir made with whole clusters and native yeast.

wines.name: Dundee Hills Pinot Noir
wines.notes: Cranberry, rose hip and spice.

wines.name: Pinot Gris
wines.notes: Pear and melon, round.

wines.name: Rosé of Pinot
wines.notes: Watermelon and lime.

events.title: Thanksgiving weekend open house
events.desc: Annual valley-wide open house with barrel tastings.

name: Lakeshore Ice Wines
story: Grapes are left on the vine until it hits −8 °C, then picked by headlamp at night.

wines.name: Riesling Icewine
wines.notes: Lychee, honey, piercing acidity.

wines.name: Cabernet Franc Icewine
wines.notes: Strawberry jam and rhubarb.

wines.name: Pinot Blanc
wines.notes: Fresh apple and lemon.

events.title: Icewine harvest night
events.desc: Volunteer pickers welcome (date depends on frost), hot soup at dawn.

name: Bodega Altos Andes
story: Vineyards at 1,100 m under the snowy Andes, watered by snowmelt canals dug by Huarpe people centuries ago.

wines.name: Malbec Reserva
wines.notes: Plum, violet and cocoa.

wines.name: Gran Malbec
wines.notes: High altitude, dense and fresh.

wines.name: Torrontés
wines.notes: Aromatic, rose and orange blossom.

events.title: Vendimia harvest festival
events.desc: Pick grapes in the morning, asado and dancing at night.

name: Viña Cordillera
story: Old Bordeaux vines brought before phylloxera, never grafted. Carmenère was rediscovered here in 1994.

wines.name: Carmenère
wines.notes: Red pepper, blackberry, smooth.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon Alto
wines.notes: Mint, cassis, firm.

wines.name: Sauvignon Blanc Costa
wines.notes: Lime and sea breeze.

events.title: Summer bike & wine
events.desc: Cycle through the vineyards with tasting stops.

name: Gumtree Creek Estate
story: Silesian settlers planted Shiraz here in the 1840s. Some of those original vines still produce fruit.

wines.name: Ancestor Shiraz
wines.notes: From 170-year-old vines: blackberry, licorice, dark chocolate.

wines.name: GSM Blend
wines.notes: Grenache, Shiraz, Mourvèdre: juicy and spicy.

wines.name: Eden Valley Riesling
wines.notes: Lime and kerosene.

events.title: Christmas long-table lunch
events.desc: Summer Christmas under the gum trees.

name: Wairau Stones
story: Stony river-bed soils and long sunny days made this valley the world capital of Sauvignon Blanc.

wines.name: Sauvignon Blanc
wines.notes: Passionfruit, gooseberry, zingy.

wines.name: Pinot Noir
wines.notes: Cherry and spice.

wines.name: Méthode Traditionnelle
wines.notes: Citrus and toast.

events.title: Summer concert in the vines
events.desc: Bring a picnic blanket; wines by the glass.

name: Klipkop Wine Farm
story: A Cape Dutch homestead under granite mountains. Home of Pinotage, a South African cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault.

wines.name: Pinotage
wines.notes: Mulberry, smoke and banana.

wines.name: Chenin Blanc Old Vine
wines.notes: Quince, honey, textured.

wines.name: Cape Blend
wines.notes: Pinotage with Cabernet, structured.

events.title: Sunset picnic & live music
events.desc: Picnic baskets on the lawn and a local band.

name: Fuji Koshu Winery
story: Vines grow on high pergolas under Mount Fuji. Koshu is Japan's own grape, delicate and pink-skinned.

wines.name: Koshu Sur Lie
wines.notes: Yuzu, white peach, gently savoury; made for sushi.

wines.name: Muscat Bailey A
wines.notes: Light, strawberry candy.

wines.name: Koshu Sparkling
wines.notes: Fine bubbles and citrus.

events.title: Hanami in the vineyard
events.desc: Cherry blossoms, bento and Koshu.

name: Château Bekaa Cèdre
story: Jesuit monks first made wine here. Caves dug by the Romans keep barrels at a steady 12 °C.

wines.name: Grand Rouge
wines.notes: Cinsault–Cabernet blend, spice and dried fig.

wines.name: Obeideh Blanc
wines.notes: Indigenous grape, almond and citrus.

wines.name: Rosé
wines.notes: Bright cherry and herbs.

events.title: Roman cave tasting
events.desc: Barrel tasting in the 2,000-year-old caves.

name: Commandaria Ktima
story: Makes Commandaria, a sun-dried sweet wine the Knights Templar shipped across Europe.

wines.name: Commandaria
wines.notes: Raisin, carob and spice.

wines.name: Xynisteri
wines.notes: Light, citrus and almond.

wines.name: Maratheftiko
wines.notes: Wild berry and herbs.

events.title: Mountain village wine walk
events.desc: Guided walk between three village cellars.

name: Dourakis Winery
story: Oenologist Andreas Dourakis founded the winery in 1988 on the hills of Alikampos, about 40 km from Chania, farming organically. Lihnos Vidiano honours his grandfather, who checked his barrels in the dark cellar by the light of a traditional Cretan oil lamp.

wines.name: Lihnos Vidiano
wines.notes: Organic Vidiano, part oak-aged: peach, apricot, honey and acacia, full and velvety.

name: Diamantakis Winery
story: A family winery in Asites, in the hills west of Heraklion, devoted to native Cretan grapes such as Vidiano and Mandilari. Its Vidiano, first made in 2011, has won major international medals.

wines.name: Vidiano
wines.notes: Peach, saffron, lemon leaves and pepper; creamy with good acidity.

wines.name: Petali Red
wines.notes: Liatiko: soft red colour, ripe fruit and firm tannins.

wines.name: Diamantopetra Red
wines.notes: Syrah and Mandilari, 12 months in oak: cherry, plum, violet and spice.

name: Silva Daskalaki Winery
story: The Daskalakis family has grown vines in the village of Siva, inside the Dafnes appellation, since 1920. In 1998 Irini Daskalaki began reviving the family vineyards, now farmed organically at 400-600 m; the name Silva comes from the village.

wines.name: Vorinos White
wines.notes: Fresh, organic Vidiano bursting with ripe nectarine.

name: Toplou Estate
story: The vineyards of the historic Toplou Monastery at the far eastern tip of Crete, farmed organically. The estate revived the ancient Thrapsathiri grape and also grows Vilana, Liatiko, Kotsifali, Assyrtiko and Syrah in windswept, dry conditions.

wines.name: Gerto Thrapsathiri
wines.notes: Organic Thrapsathiri: lemon blossom, grapefruit, pineapple and mango.

name: Th{eros} Wines Collectiva
story: A wine collective started in 2020 by Konstantinos Manouras to showcase native Cretan grapes and the vineyards that grow them, such as Plyto, Thrapsathiri, Vidiano and Mandilari.

wines.name: Thrapsathiri
wines.notes: Native Cretan white from a single variety.

wines.name: Φ-Low Mandilari Nouveau
wines.notes: Light, early-release Mandilari.

name: Antonopoulos Vineyards
story: Konstantinos Antonopoulos planted his first vines in 1983 high in the mountains of Achaia, ringed by Panachaikos, Helmos and Erymanthos, and helped establish the area as a wine zone. Since 1994 the company has been owned by the Chalkias family; vineyards run from 150 to 950 m.

wines.name: Adoli Ghis White
wines.notes: Lagorthi, Roditis and Chardonnay from 750-900 m: fresh yellow fruit and chamomile.

wines.name: Anax Chardonnay
wines.notes: Barrel-fermented mountain Chardonnay, rich and concentrated.

wines.name: Morfeas
wines.notes: Their age-worthy red blend.

name: Aivalis Winery
story: Christos Aivalis makes some of Nemea's most sought-after reds. He farms without fertiliser or irrigation so roots dig deep, vinifies each vineyard separately and bottles unfined and unfiltered. Monopati, from vines over 50 years old, was his first top wine.

wines.name: Monopati
wines.notes: Agiorgitiko from 50+ year-old vines: concentrated, oak-aged and long-lived.

name: Mitravelas Estate
story: One of Nemea's oldest wine families, recorded since 1828; the first family winery opened in the centre of Nemea in 1913. Today they farm about 10 ha of their own plus growers' vineyards in Ahladi, Tzintari, Agios Dimitrios and Koutsi.

wines.name: Red on Black
wines.notes: Fresh, unoaked Agiorgitiko: a cherry bomb in the glass.

wines.name: Nemea
wines.notes: Classic Agiorgitiko: red fruit jam, pepper, leather and vanilla.

wines.name: Nemea Old Vines
wines.notes: Ultra-concentrated Agiorgitiko from two vineyards over 55 years old.

name: Moropoulos Winery
story: A grape-growing family from Neochori in the Mantinia plateau who began bottling their own wine in 2015, led by siblings Georgia and Kostas. They explore Moschofilero in many styles, from fresh and rosé to late-release, sparkling and the single-vineyard '72'.

wines.name: Mantinia Moschofilero
wines.notes: Rich, concentrated Moschofilero with sharp acidity.

wines.name: Moschofilero Rosé
wines.notes: Moschofilero made as a rosé: cherries, raspberries and lift.

wines.name: 72 Mantinia
wines.notes: Single vineyard planted in 1972, part aged in amphora and acacia.

name: Avantis Estate
story: The family's story begins in the 19th century, when Anastasios Mountrichas bought land at Afrati in central Evia. Today oenologists Apostolos Mountrichas and his wife Lenga farm about 20 ha on steep south-east slopes at 250-500 m, from Malagousia and Assyrtiko to Syrah and Gewurztraminer.

wines.name: Lenga Gewurztraminer
wines.notes: Aromatic, slightly off-dry Gewurztraminer: acacia, geranium, ginger.

wines.name: Lenga Pink
wines.notes: Mavrokountoura with Gewurztraminer, salmon pink and perfumed.

wines.name: Sauvignon Blanc
wines.notes: Lemon, apple and lime; easy and cool.

wines.name: Agios Chronos Red
wines.notes: Syrah with a touch of Viognier, a year in new French oak.

name: Domaine Katsaros
story: Doctor Dimitris Katsaros and his wife Stella revived winegrowing at Krania, 700 m up on the eastern slopes of Mount Olympus, in the 1980s, planting Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay. Their first wine came out in 1987, and the red is often called the 'Greek Bordeaux'.

wines.name: Katsaros Red
wines.notes: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot from 700 m: cherry, raspberry and fine oak.

wines.name: Chardonnay
wines.notes: Mountain Chardonnay from the eastern foothills of Olympus.

wines.name: Valos
wines.notes: Their younger red.

name: Theopetra Estate (Tsililis)
story: The Tsililis family replanted the phylloxera-hit vineyards of Meteora in 1995, on the slopes around the prehistoric Theopetra cave, where ancient grape seeds have been found. Today about 10 ha are farmed organically, with local Limniona alongside Xinomavro and international grapes.

wines.name: Limniona
wines.notes: Crimson jam, prunes, violet and spice; firm tannins, sharp acidity.

wines.name: Theopetra Red
wines.notes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Limniona: blackcurrant, sour cherry and pepper.

wines.name: Theopetra Rosé
wines.notes: Cherry, strawberry, rose and spice.

wines.name: Xinomavro Rosé
wines.notes: Organic Xinomavro rosé, 40 days on lees.
